metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Essex County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Horseneck & Passaic Valley District, Two Bridges & Passaic River District
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 1.89%, with an equalization ratio of 87.2%.
Public education represents 48.6% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 35.2%.
Average residential assessment is $549,360, producing an average annual tax bill of $10,382.9.

neighborhoods.name: Horseneck & Passaic Valley District
neighborhoods.character: Expansive single-family ranches, split-levels, and colonials on large lots, surrounded by major corporate and industrial parks
neighborhoods.description: Northwest Essex township known for low residential taxes due to massive industrial warehouse and Route 46 commercial corridors.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Enjoys lowest property tax rate in Essex County (1.854% certified) with commercial ratables footing over 58% of the levy.

neighborhoods.name: Two Bridges & Passaic River District
neighborhoods.character: Suburban single-family residences and ranches on generous lots near Two Bridges confluence
neighborhoods.description: Quiet residential enclave with spacious properties and proximity to West Essex regional high school.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Enjoys extraordinary tax advantages from Fairfield's commercial and industrial ratables.

equityAnalysis.summary: Fairfield Township maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Fairfield Township, homeowners pay an average of $10,382.9 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 8.09% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 87.2%, assessed values average ~87.2% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 48.6% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 35.2%, and Essex County claims 16.2%.
